0.title: APIs and Data Exchange
0.summary: Follow one application asking an invoice service for work, then expand that simple conversation into the real rules an API needs: operations, inputs, responses, errors, security, retries, pagination, webhooks, GraphQL, events, and safe change over time.

1.title: Deployment and Hosting
1.summary: Start with one production build, then follow artifact creation, configuration, hosting choices, domains, HTTPS, release pipelines, observability, rollback, and the failure stages that make deployment diagnosable.

2.title: Git and GitHub
2.summary: Learn Git by following a project through real state changes: edit files, choose what belongs in the next saved snapshot, commit it, branch safely, share it with another repository, review it on GitHub, automate checks, and recover from mistakes.

3.title: How the Web Works
3.summary: Follow what actually happens after you enter a web address: the browser finds the destination, creates a protected connection, asks for resources, receives a response, and turns the result into a page.

4.title: HTML, CSS, and JavaScript
4.summary: Learn the three core browser languages by building one small page: HTML gives content meaning and structure, CSS controls presentation and layout, and JavaScript adds behavior when the page needs to react or change.

5.title: Node.js and Package Management
5.summary: Start with one JavaScript file that needs to run outside the browser, then learn how Node.js executes it, how package.json describes a project, how package managers resolve dependencies, why lockfiles matter, how ESM and CommonJS differ, and how to keep installs secure and reproducible.

6.title: React
6.summary: Build one small interactive interface from components and props, then follow React’s actual model through events, state snapshots, render and commit, shared state, identity, effects, refs, external systems, performance decisions, accessibility, and production failure states.

7.title: Security and Authentication
7.summary: Start with a request carrying untrusted input, then follow identity, permission, sessions, browser protections, password storage, common attacks, and practical evidence for finding and fixing security failures.

8.title: Testing and Quality
8.summary: Start with a small behavior that can break, write an observable check for it, then expand into test boundaries, assertions, doubles, browser interaction, coverage, flaky failures, and a maintainable verification pipeline.

9.title: The 7 Types of Databases
9.summary: Learn seven practical database families by starting with familiar data questions—orders, nested content, sessions, relationships, measurements, text search, and similarity—then continue into schemas, transactions, indexes, consistency, specialized stores, and production trade-offs.

10.title: TypeScript
10.summary: Begin with an ordinary JavaScript bug caused by an unexpected value, then learn how TypeScript describes possible values, infers types, narrows unions, models objects and functions, uses generics, resolves modules, and separates compile-time confidence from runtime validation.

11.title: Vite
11.summary: Start with the practical problem of serving many modern frontend modules during development, then learn Vite’s dev server, ESM module graph, HMR, dependency handling, asset transforms, TypeScript transpilation boundary, configuration, plugins, environment modes, production build, base paths, code splitting, and deployment diagnosis.
